examples.label: Fingerprint WordPress in the page source
List referenced plugins (paths leak plugin + version)
Read a plugin readme.txt to confirm its exact version

recommended.note: If the Mail Masta plugin is present, go straight for its LFI.
If wpDiscuz is present, target its unauthenticated RCE.

name: WordPress - Detect and Enumerate via cURL
description: Confirms a WordPress install and passively enumerates active themes and plugins from asset links in the page source. Plugin readme.txt files often leak versions for CVE matching.

defense.why_it_works: WordPress embeds version-revealing strings in page source (/wp-content/ paths, generator meta tag, readme.html, /wp-login.php). Plugin readme.txt files expose exact plugin versions. All are publicly readable without authentication.
defense.prerequisites: HTTP access to the WordPress site. No credentials required.
defense.impact: Attacker confirms CMS type and version, discovers active plugins and themes, and maps exact CVE candidates before any active exploitation attempt.
defense.detection: Automated requests to /wp-login.php, /readme.html, /wp-content/plugins/*/readme.txt in rapid succession. IDS signatures for WPScan-style probing.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (GET /wp-login.php, /readme.html from single IP) | WAF alerts for CMS fingerprinting patterns
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype=access_combined (uri_path=\"/wp-login.php\" OR uri_path=\"/wp-content/\" OR uri_path=\"/readme.html\")
| stats count dc(uri_path) as urls by clientip, useragent, bin(_time, 1m)
| where urls>20 OR count>100
defense.elastic_kql: event.category:web AND source.ip:* AND url.path:("/wp-login.php" OR "/wp-content/" OR "/readme.html")
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| summarize urls=dcount(csUriStem), hits=count() by cIP, csUserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where urls > 20 or hits > 100
| sort by hits desc
// wordpress application fingerprinting/enumeration (path burst, scanner UA)
defense.prevention: Remove readme.html, license.txt from the web root. Suppress WordPress version in the generator meta tag (remove_action). Block /wp-content/ direct file access where possible. Use WordFence to detect enumeration attempts.
defense.misconfiguration: WordPress served with default readme.html and no version suppression, exposing exact version in the generator tag and /wp-includes/version.php readable via direct access.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# WordPress default
# <meta name="generator" content="WordPress 5.8.1"/>
# readme.html accessible at webroot
# /wp-includes/version.php readable
defense.evasion: Read plugin list from page source JS (no direct /readme.txt hits). Use Google dorking (site:target.com inurl:wp-content) instead of active probing.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review IIS Web Server logs, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Detects WordPress and enumerates themes/plugins from the page source:
  curl -s http://<url>/   fetch the homepage
  | grep -E 'WordPress|themes|plugins'   pull WordPress markers and asset links
Confirms the CMS and reveals active themes/plugins passively; a plugin's /wp-content/plugins/<name>/readme.txt usually leaks its version for CVE matching.
